3. Treat the renamed implementation and test files as moves. Their meaningful edits are limited to crate paths and normalizing the new crate's type names to `HttpClient` and `RequestBuilder`.
4. Review `codex-rs/Cargo.toml`, `codex-rs/Cargo.lock`, and the two `BUILD.bazel` files as mechanical workspace integration.


### What issue are you seeing?

When Codex is launched normally from a terminal inside a repo, the `/resume` picker correctly shows both filter modes:

- `[Cwd]`
- `All`

However, when Codex is launched through a remote App Server flow, the active cwd is displayed correctly in the Codex status line, but the `/resume` picker only shows:

- `[All]`

This happens even though the remote TUI is launched with an explicit cwd using `--cd`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start a Codex App Server.
2. Launch a remote Codex TUI with an explicit cwd:

   ```bash
   codex --remote ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --cd /path/to/repo
   ```

3. Confirm the TUI status line shows `/path/to/repo`.
4. Open `/resume`.
5. Observe that the picker only shows `Filter: [All]`, not `Filter: [Cwd] All`.

For comparison:

```bash
cd /path/to/repo
codex
```

Then opening `/resume` shows the expected `[Cwd]` filter.

### What is the expected behavior?

If Codex is launched with:

```bash
codex --remote ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --cd /path/to/repo
```

then `/resume` should treat `/path/to/repo` as the current working directory and show the `[Cwd]` filter option, the same way plain `codex` or `codex resume` does when started from that directory.

### Additional information

From reading the current source, the resume picker only shows `[Cwd]` when its `filter_cwd` is populated. For remote workspaces, `filter_cwd` appears to come from `app_server.remote_cwd_override()`.

The main remote TUI session receives `remote_cwd_override` from `--cd`, but when `/resume` is opened from an existing session, Codex starts a separate picker App Server session via `start_app_server_for_picker(...)`. That picker session does not appear to receive the existing remote cwd override, so `filter_cwd` ends up `None`, causing the picker to collapse to `Filter: [All]`.

Relevant areas I looked at:

- `tui/src/resume_picker.rs`
- `tui/src/app/event_dispatch.rs`
- `tui/src/lib.rs`
- `tui/src/app_server_session.rs`

items.title: feat(thread-store): load bounded model context for resume
items.body:
## Description

This PR adds a storage-level API for loading the rollout items needed to reconstruct the latest model-visible context without loading an entire thread history.

For paginated local threads, the store reads the canonical `SessionMeta` from the rollout head and reverse-scans plain JSONL files from EOF to the latest usable replacement-history checkpoint.

## Why

Paginated thread resume needs a bounded model-context path before large threads can resume without hydrating the full rollout.

Legacy and unsupported rollout shapes stay on the existing full-history path so reconstruction semantics remain unchanged while the app-server resume wiring lands separately.

## What changed

- Added `ThreadStore::load_latest_model_context` and `StoredModelContext`.
- Added local reverse JSONL scanning that selects the latest usable `CompactedItem` plus the turn metadata needed for resume reconstruction.
- Preserved canonical `SessionMeta` at the front of the returned replay items.
- Falls back to full history for legacy threads, compressed rollouts, missing `replacement_history`, rollback markers, and ambiguous boundaries.
- Added in-memory store support for callers that do not have a targeted storage read.
- Added focused tests for checkpoint selection, conservative fallback, and malformed tail lines.

## Validation

- `just test -p codex-thread-store`
- `just fix -p codex-thread-store`

## Follow-up

The paginated app-server `thread/resume` path still needs to consume this API. Compressed rollouts continue to use the full-history fallback for now.

items.title: [apps] route MCP resource reads by originating tool call
items.body:
## Why

Codex Apps share the `codex_apps` MCP server and may legitimately publish the same widget resource URI. Because `mcpServer/resource/read` currently identifies resources only by thread, server, and URI, plugin-runtime can return one app’s widget HTML for another app’s tool call.

Client-side cache isolation prevents cross-app response reuse but cannot disambiguate the initial resource read. This PR adds that server-side routing.

## What changes

- Adds an optional `originCallId` to `mcpServer/resource/read`.
- Resolves it against trusted tool-call context from the active turn or persisted thread history.
- Validates the server, resource URI, connector, link, and route against current server-owned tool metadata.
- Routes plugin-runtime reads through the originating app’s `fetch_resource` path.
- Keeps existing `resources/read` behavior for requests without an origin, non-Codex Apps servers, and legacy implementations.
- Updates the generated schemas, TypeScript types, and app-server documentation.

Clients pass only the opaque call ID; app-server owns routing metadata construction and validation.

## Integration

The Codex webview must send `originCallId: item.callId` with the existing `threadId`. Cache isolation and origin-aware routing address separate failure modes: cache isolation prevents response reuse, while this change ensures fresh reads reach the originating app.

## Coverage

Tests cover colliding resource URIs, persisted and ephemeral threads, identity mismatches, legacy fallback behavior, and authoritative live tool metadata.

items.title: feat(core): emit canonical collab wait items
items.body:
This PR depends on [#31296](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/31296) for the canonical-to-legacy event mappings.

## Description

This PR makes the v1 and v2 wait paths emit canonical `TurnItem::CollabAgentToolCall` lifecycle instead of `CollabWaitingBegin` / `CollabWaitingEnd` directly.

Both paths already used the same legacy waiting events before this PR. The v1 item carries receiver metadata and final agent statuses for its target agents; v2 waits for mailbox activity rather than specific agents, so it keeps those fields empty, matching the existing v2 legacy payload.

App-server v2 consumes the canonical item directly and ignores the mapped legacy wait events.

## Why

Wait is separate from the other collab tools because it is multi-target and has distinct timeout/status behavior. Keeping it last also lets this PR remove the old helper that only existed to shape legacy wait status entries in core.

## What changed

- Emit canonical collab wait items from both v1 and v2 wait handlers.
- Preserve receiver metadata and agent status snapshots on completed wait items.
- Remove the old core helper for building legacy wait status entries.

## Follow-up

The next stack PR, [#30188](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/30188), writes canonical `TurnItem` values to paginated rollout files.
